He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. He was selected 10th overall by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the first round of the [[2019 NBA draft]]. Coming out of high school, Reddish was rated as a five-star recruit and considered one of the top players in his class, earning [[Mr. and Miss Pennsylvania Basketball|Mr. Pennsylvania Basketball]] in his senior year, in addition to being named to the [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]], 2018 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and 2018 [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. ==High school career== Reddish attended the [[Haverford School]] in [[Haverford, Pennsylvania]], as a freshman before transferring to [[Westtown School]] in [[West Chester, Pennsylvania]], where he teamed up with Class of 2017 five-star recruit and current NBA player [[Mohamed Bamba]].{{Cite news|url= https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/10/cam-reddish-westtown-high-school-duke-basketball-recruit|title=Duke-bound Cam Reddish could reset expectations for the modern basketball player|last=Johnson|first=Chris|date=March 10, 2018|work=si.com|access-date=October 31, 2019}} As a junior, Reddish averaged 16.2 points per game and led the Moose to a Friend's School League title.{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/cameron-reddish/#qeuGaP4EiE8bE3C1.97|website=slamonline.com|title=Grindin' My Whole Life: Cameron Reddish |access-date=December 27, 2017}} During the summer of 2017, Reddish averaged 23.8 points, 7.6 rebounds and 3.1 assists for his [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team, Team Final, on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League|Nike EYBL Circuit]]. Later that summer, he played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team]].{{cite web|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/philly-hoops/duke-basketball-cam-reddish-westtown-school-under-19-world-championships-20170908.html|title=Duke-bound Cam Reddish and his crazy summer {{pipe}} Mike Jensen|website=philly.com|access-date=December 27, 2017}} He was originally going to play for the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|under-17]] team the previous summer, but did not make the team due to injury.{{cite web|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/cameron-reddish-team-usa-basketball-roster-westtown|title=Elite forward Cameron Reddish misses Team USA roster because of injury, but he'll be back {{pipe}} USA TODAY High School Sports|website=usatodayhss.com|access-date=December 27, 2017}} In his senior year, he averaged 22.6 points and 5.6 rebounds per game. After his senior season, he was named 2018 [[Mr. and Miss Pennsylvania Basketball|Mr. Pennsylvania Basketball]].{{Cite news |date=May 26, 2018 |title=Duke signee, Westtown star Cam Reddish named Mr. PA Basketball |work=pennlive.com |url=https://www.pennlive.com/highschoolsports/article/duke-signee-westtown-star-cam-reddish-named-mr-pa-basketball |access-date=October 31, 2019}} Reddish was selected to play in the 2018 [[McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]], and [[Nike Hoop Summit]] All-Star games.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2018/3/27/17165100/mcdonalds-all-americans-game-2018-duke-zion-williamson-rj-barrett-cameron-reddish-bol-bol|title=Meet the 2018 McDonald's All-Americans, led by Duke's trio of Superstar trio of recruits|work=sbnation.com|access-date=March 27, 2018}} ===Recruiting=== Reddish was a five-star recruit. ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Hawks (2019–2022)=== On June 20, 2019, Reddish was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 10th overall pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{Cite news |last=Newberry Reddish officially signed with the Hawks.{{cite web |last=Bowers |first=Andrew |date=July 1, 2019 |title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Cam Reddish |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-sign-cam-reddish |access-date=July 1, 2019 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On October 24, 2019, Reddish made his [[NBA]] debut, started in a 117–100 win over the [[2019–20 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]] with season|Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hawks-cam-reddish-career-best-performance/|title=Hawks' Cam Reddish: Career-best performance|website=CBS Sports|date=December 22, 2021|access-date=December 28, 2021}} ===New York Knicks (2022–2023)=== On January 13, 2022, the Hawks traded Reddish, along with [[Solomon Hill (basketball)|Solomon Hill]], a 2025 second-round draft pick and cash considerations, to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for future teammate [[Kevin Knox II]] and a protected future first-round pick.{{cite web |title=Knicks Acquire Cam Reddish |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-acquire-cam-reddish |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 14, 2022 |date=January 13, 2022}}{{cite web |last=Rehmann |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-kevin-knox-ii-and-first-round-pick-exchange-cam-reddish-solomon-hill-and-second-round |access-date=January 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} Reddish made his Knicks debut on January 23, 2022, logging two points and two rebounds in five minutes.{{Cite news|last=Berman|first=Marc|title=Cam Reddish not likely to remain in Knicks' rotation despite first Knicks announced that Reddish would miss the rest of the season due to a right shoulder injury.{{cite web|title=Knicks' Cam Reddish out for season with shoulder [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |date=February 9, 2023 |title=Portland Completes Multi-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/portland-completes-multi-team-trade |access-date=February 9, Knecht]] were traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Mark Williams (basketball)|Mark Williams]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-acquire-dalton-knecht-cam-reddish-first-round-draft-pick-and-pick-swap-from-los-angeles-lakers|title=Charlotte Hornets Acquire Dalton Knecht, On March 27, the Lakers announced that they had waived Reddish.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-27 |title=Los Angeles Lakers Release Player After Pacers Game |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/los-angeles-lakers-release-player-after-pacers-game-reddish-nba-news |access-date=2025-03-28 |website=Fastbreak On SI |language=en-US |archive-date=March 27, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250327212925/https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/los-angeles-lakers-release-player-after-pacers-game-reddish-nba-news |url-status=dead }} === Šiauliai (2025) === On September 10, 2025, Reddish signed with [[BC Šiauliai|Šiauliai]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] (LKL).{{Cite web |date=2025-09-10 |title=Šiauliuose – dviženklį taškų vidurkį NBA rinkęs žaidėjas |url=https://bcsiauliai.lt/siauliuose-dvizenkli-tasku-vidurki-nba-rinkes-zaidejas/ |access-date=2025-09-22 |website=bcsiauliai.lt |language=lt}} On December 6, Reddish left Šiauliai by a mutual agreement, and returned to the U.S. for personal reasons.{{Cite web |date=2025-12-06 |title="Šiaulių" klubas atsisveikina su Camu Reddishu |url=https://bcsiauliai.lt/siauliu-klubas-atsisveikina-su-camu-reddishu/ |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=bcsiauliai.lt |language=lt}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2026)=== On January 21, 2026, Reddish was assigned to the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]];
